messages:
sam: deploy-bot blocked a publish to prod for v1.12.3 — error says 'intermediate layer rewrite detected'. tagging stopped. anyone oncall to triage?

deploy-bot: publish rejected: layer digest mismatch for layer index 3. expected sha256:4a7f...c1 got sha256:9d3b...7f. provenance attestation refused. CI build id 2026-03-20T09:10Z.

ci-bot: quick log paste:
```
[push] uploading layer 3/7
[push] upload completed: 9d3b...7f
[manifest] creating manifest referencing layers: [sha256:... 9d3b...7f ...]
[verify] provenance-check failed: remote manifest digest mismatch vs attestation
ERROR: publish failed: intermediate layer rewrite (dedupe-squash mismatch)
```

aleks: hmm. this smells like the registry deduped a layer and recomputed the digest when we rebase the image. did the build process run with buildkit layer squashing?

sana: @aleks we did enable inline cache during the build to speed up CI. Could be a cache-export change that rewrote metadata.

kai: impact question: is this only blocking promotion to prod, or also canary?

sam: only prod got blocked — canary already has the previous digest (sha256:aa11...). release pipeline halted at promotion step.

zara: options: 1) retag previous published digest (pin) and proceed with release using the known-good image; 2) force-publish the newly built image after re-running build with cache disabled and re-attest; 3) patch attestation to accept the rewrite (no). I vote for pin+republish later in a controlled window.

aleks: +1 to pin. Forcing attestation changes is unsafe. Also, forcing a publish now risks drift between what prod runs and what we test.

sam: agreement from oncall? @kai?

kai: pin is safest. I'll open a hotfix PR to update the release metadata to point to sha256:aa11... and skip promotion step. Hold on doing any rolling deploys until we confirm.

ci-bot: command to retag in case we need manual: 
```
aws ecr put-image --repository-name redwood/api --image-tag v1.12.3 --image-manifest "$(aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name redwood/api --image-ids imageDigest=sha256:aa11... --query images[0].imageManifest --output text)"
```

sam: adding change window: propose 2-hour window at 14:00 UTC to re-run clean builds and republish with attestation. who can own the republish?

aleks: I can take republish. I'll run with `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0` and explicitly clear cache, then create new attestation and push to staging for validation.

sana: I'll update the release notes draft and call out this as "metadata republish — no functional changes" and include the pinned digest used for prod.

zara: also update the deploybot exemptions list? we should avoid exceptions but add a note in the change log so SRE knows why we pinned.

sam: final decision: pin prod to sha256:aa11... now, proceed with canary unchanged, schedule republish at 14:00 UTC. No automatic rollouts during the republish window.

deploy-bot: manual override accepted by @kai. Promotion resumed for pinned digest.

kai: executing pin now. will follow up when done. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. once republish completes @aleks please post new manifest, attestation, and the small verification snippet to this thread so we can close out.

aleks: will do.

zara: noted for release notes and internal changelog.

sam: closing the coordination thread — followups in #incidents if anything regresses.
